findings.title: Unsupported paginator option causes optimized requests to fail before pagination
findings.body: `self.paginate` does not accept or forward an `enable_advanced_features` keyword to paginator constructors. Since no pagination plumbing was changed to support this new argument, an authorized request with `optimized_pagination=true` raises `TypeError` at this call instead of constructing `OptimizedCursorPaginator`, resulting in a 500 response. Extend the shared pagination API to pass an explicit constructor option, or remove/configure this option without passing it to `paginate`.

findings.title: Optimized paginator treats AuditLogEntry datetime keys as numeric values
findings.body: The audit-log endpoint instantiates this paginator with `order_by="-datetime"`, where `AuditLogEntry.datetime` is a `datetime`. On every non-empty first page, cursor construction calls `get_item_key`, and `math.floor`/`math.ceil` on that datetime raises `TypeError`. Even if that conversion were avoided, `value_from_cursor` leaves the generated numeric cursor value as an integer, so subsequent queryset filtering compares the datetime column with an integer. The optimized paginator needs DateTimePaginator-compatible key and cursor-value conversion (for example, by subclassing `DateTimePaginator`) for this endpoint to work.

findings.title: Negative offsets are not supported by Django QuerySet slicing
findings.body: This branch passes a negative `start_offset` directly to `queryset[start_offset:stop]`, but Django QuerySets reject negative indexing and slicing with `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported.` `Cursor.from_string` accepts signed integer offsets, so an authorized caller can request an optimized cursor such as `0:-1:0` and receive a 500 instead of the advertised reverse-pagination behavior. Validate/reject negative offsets or implement reverse traversal using supported queryset bounds; they cannot be used as Python-style negative slices on a QuerySet.
